scores.evidence: MVP: Catalog, flat-rate subscriptions, invoices, one PSP, basic ledger, webhooks, pooled tenancy with RLS.
scores.rationale: Phases roughly go simple to complex, but the ledger is only 'basic' in MVP and nothing is proven before dependents are built; cell isolation lands in Phase 3 after the core is built.

scores.evidence: MVP: Catalog, flat-rate subscriptions, invoices, one PSP, basic ledger, webhooks, pooled tenancy with RLS.
scores.rationale: The MVP is a thin-ish end-to-end slice, but it is a feature bundle with no claim of production deployment, CI/CD, or a first thin path.

scores.evidence: Pooled model with RLS by default... 'If billing isn't your core product, use Stripe Billing, Orb, Metronome, or Lago'
scores.rationale: Defaults and some conditions (tenancy tiers, build vs buy, modular monolith) appear, but there is no consolidated irreversible-decision list with explicit flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Split out only Usage Metering and Payments first. Those two have the most different scaling and risk profiles.
scores.rationale: Some blast-radius reasoning exists (tenancy enforcement, ledger core), but the phases do not order work by widest impact.
Security is thorough in a standalone section and MVP has RLS, but it is not described per phase.

scores.evidence: Trace IDs follow a request through events, PSP calls, and webhooks.
scores.rationale: Observability is a standalone section and is not placed in the MVP or tied to any phase.
Replay, re-rating, and raw event retention are reproducibility-minded, and Terraform is listed, but nothing is threaded through the phases.

scores.evidence: Idempotency at every boundary: API, consumers (dedupe by event ID), and PSP calls.
scores.rationale: Resilience is strong in a dedicated section, but the phases do not say when it arrives, and dunning and DR are not phased.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so it does not declare the layer N/A.

scores.evidence: Phase 4: Marketplace payouts, data residency, a quoting and CPQ integration, and advanced analytics.
scores.rationale: Later phases show what is deferred, but there are no pull-forward conditions.

note: A technically strong billing architecture, but it is organized by subsystem rather than by build order. Cross-cutting concerns are standalone sections, and the plan has no decision gates, pull-forward conditions, or AI N/A statement.
